title: Emoji face
summary: CSS art: a shaded round face with eyes, rosy cheeks and a smile made from one border.
brief: Centre a 200px round face in the stage. It is shaded with a radial gradient: #fef08a lit from 35% across and 30% down, through #facc15 at 60%, to #eab308 at the edge. It has a soft drop shadow and a slightly darker inner bottom edge.
The eyes are 20 × 30px ovals, 64px from the top of the face, 58px in from each side. The cheeks are 36 × 20px blurred pink ovals at 60% opacity, 110px from the top and 28px in from each side.
The smile is a single shape: a 100 × 50px box 96px from the top and 50px from the left, whose only visible part is an 8px #422006 bottom border curved into an arc.
hints: display: grid and place-items: center on .stage centre the face. The face is position: relative so the features can be placed with absolute offsets inside it.
For the shading use background-image: radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%, #fef08a, #facc15 60%, #eab308). Blur the cheeks with filter: blur(4px).
The smile: border-bottom: 8px solid #422006 with border-radius: 0 0 50px 50px. Rounding only the bottom corners bends the bottom border into a curve that thins out at the ends.
solutionNotes: The face is one element with layered paint: a radial gradient off-centre fakes a light source, an inset shadow darkens the bottom edge and an outer shadow lifts it off the page. Every feature is absolutely positioned inside it, and the pairs share a class for size and only differ in left or right, so they stay symmetrical. The smile is the clever part: a box with only a bottom border, whose bottom corners are rounded by half its width, bends that border into an arc that tapers where the invisible side borders would be.
